name: Separate immediate approval from the quality criterion
decision_structure: Familiar, conventional writing receives immediate approval while more independent writing produces friction. The writer must decide whether current audience approval is the objective or merely one signal among several.
rule: Before optimizing for applause, define the article's quality objective. If immediate approval rewards formulaic language that conflicts with the objective, do not use popularity as the sole editing criterion; if reach and comprehension are core objectives, treat reader response as legitimate evidence instead of dismissing it.
operational_actions: Separate readability metrics from originality and argument-quality metrics.
Identify which familiar formulas help navigation and which only imitate prevailing taste.
When a passage is unpopular, diagnose whether the problem is valuable unfamiliarity or simply poor communication.
boundary_conditions: Platform writing often has explicit reach objectives.
Reader confusion is not evidence of profundity.
Historical rejection by contemporaries does not automatically predict long-term value.
failure_signals: The advisor treats low engagement as proof of quality.
The advisor dismisses all audience feedback as conformity pressure.

specificity.writer_added_delta: Han Yu's first-person contrast makes audience approval itself an object of diagnosis rather than a default quality label, but the modern metric framework is a transfer inference.

composition_audit.alternative_interpretation: The letter may be rhetorical self-fashioning; modern platform goals differ sharply from Han Yu's stated ambitions.
